title: Hokuzan
capsule: Hokuzan (北山, Kingdom of Sanhoku) was the northernmost of the three kingdoms that divided Okinawa during the Sanzan period, established around 1314 when regional lords of the island's northern districts consolidated independent rule centered on Nakijin Castle. The kingdom sent tributary missions to Ming China from the 1370s, competing commercially with the rival central kingdom of Chūzan. Internal defections among Hokuzan's vassals fatally weakened it in the 1410s, and Chūzan's king Shō Hashi stormed Nakijin Castle in 1416; the last king and his inner circle committed suicide rather than surrender. Shō Hashi installed his son Shō Chū as warden of the former territory in 1422, reducing Hokuzan to an administrative division of what became the unified Ryukyu Kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The broad outline of the Sanzan kingdoms is well-documented through Ryukyuan chronicles and Ming records, but precise internal borders between Hokuzan, Chūzan, and Nanzan are only approximately reconstructed from textual sources with no surviving cadastral mapping.
